# Medication normalizer

<!-- Generated by ml/train.py. Do not edit by hand; re-run the trainer. -->

Character n-gram TF-IDF into multinomial logistic regression. 2759 features, fitted in 0.9s on 2144 synthetic examples, evaluated on 896 held-out ones.

```bash
pip install -r requirements-bench.txt
python -m ml.train
```

## Results

| Approach | Known-drug accuracy | Unknown correctly rejected | False-accept rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rules only (shipped baseline) | 0.969 | 0.975 | 0.025 |
| Exact dictionary only (no fuzzy) | 0.662 | 1.000 | 0.000 |
| Model only | 0.625 | 1.000 | 0.000 |
| Rules then model | 0.981 | 0.975 | 0.025 |
| Exact, model-vetoed fuzzy | 0.834 | 1.000 | 0.000 |

**False-accept rate is the metric that matters.** It is the share of drugs this
project does not cover that were nonetheless assigned a drug class. Every false
accept is a potential missed interaction presented as a confident answer, so the
operating point is chosen on this column rather than on accuracy.

## Threshold sweep

| Threshold | Known accuracy | False-accept rate |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 0.740 | 0.006 |
| 0.3 | 0.721 | 0.006 |
| 0.5 | 0.666 | 0.006 |
| 0.6 | 0.625 | 0.000 |
| 0.7 | 0.557 | 0.000 |
| 0.8 | 0.482 | 0.000 |
| 0.9 | 0.368 | 0.000 |

Shipped threshold: **0.6**. Below it the model declines to answer
and the entry is treated as unrecognized, which makes the profile incomplete and
withholds any personalized verdict.

## Held-out drugs

14 of 71 names were excluded from training entirely, so their score measures generalisation to an unseen name rather than
memorisation: ativan, ciprofloxacin, clozaril, coumadin, doxycycline, fosamax, levofloxacin, lisinopril, prinivil, restoril, rivaroxaban, tramadol, vicodin, zolpidem.

## Why not a transformer

The task is a few thousand short strings over 15 classes, and the noise is
character-level. n-grams model that directly, train in seconds, and export to
plain JSON (496 KB) so runtime inference needs no ML dependency at all.
